message.content: In Christian theology, **Jesus Christ** is regarded as the most important prophet—and indeed the central figure of the faith. Christians believe that Jesus is the fulfillment of the Old‑Testament prophecies, the promised Messiah, and the Son of God who came to bring salvation. While other prophets such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and John the Baptist are highly respected and play crucial roles in the biblical narrative, Jesus is considered the ultimate prophet whose life, teachings, death, and resurrection form the foundation of Christian belief.
